title: On the triviality of the unramified Iwasawa modules of the maximal multiple $ mathbb{Z} p$-extensions

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 1 (Introduction), statement of the Generalized Greenberg Conjecture
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper writes: "X(k̃) is a pseudo-null Z_p[[Gal(k̃/k)]]-module. In other words, X(k̃) is conjectured such that any prime ideal with height less than 2 annihilates X(k̃)." This is mathematically false: pseudo-nullity means the annihilator ideal has height ≥ 2 (equivalently, X localized at every height-1 prime vanishes, i.e. no prime of height ≤ 1 contains the annihilator). As literally stated, the zero ideal (height 0) would annihilate X(k̃), which forces X(k̃)=0.

The presentation matrix A' is explicitly displayed as a 4×4 matrix (rows/columns indexed by γ,x,y,z), so A(k)=coker is trivial iff rank(A' mod p)=4, cyclic iff rank 3, and dim A(k)/pA(k)=2 iff rank 2. The text instead asserts "A(k)=0 ⟺ rank Ā' = 3, A(k) cyclic ⟺ rank Ā' = 2, dim = 2 ⟺ rank Ā' = 1", which is off by one (these would be the correct ranks for the 3×3 block A, not for A'). Compare with the correct degree-4 analogue in Corollary 3.1.5, where the matrix really is 3×3 and ranks 3,2,1 are used.

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 4.1.8, last line of the proof
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The lemma states "K(G)=0 if and only if |K| ≢ 0 (mod p)", and K(G)=0 is equivalent to the presentation matrix having full rank 6, i.e. to the displayed 3×3 determinant being a unit. The proof however concludes "K(G)=0 if and only if −det[…] = (a+b+c)³+(a+b−c)³ ≡ 0 (mod p)", i.e. the opposite (non)vanishing condition, contradicting both the lemma statement and the later use in Lemma 4.2.2 ("we only need to show that |K| = 2(a+b)((a+b)²+3c²) ≢ 0").

After substituting the hypotheses the proof obtains |K| ≡ 2(a+b)c(a−b+c) in the case c ≢ 0, and then writes "Since a−b+c ≢ 0 and a+b ≢ 0, we obtain |K| ≢ 0 in the case c ≡ 0." The case c ≡ 0 was already treated in the previous sentence, and the displayed product is nonzero precisely because c ≢ 0; the conclusion is stated for the wrong case.

The paper asserts k_∞ ↔ ⟨γx^{a−c}, xy^{−1}z, xy⟩ = ⟨J(γ)γ, xy^{−1}z, xy⟩. Modulo ⟨xy, xy^{−1}z⟩ one has y ≡ x^{−1}, z ≡ x^{−2}, so J(γ)γ ≡ γ²x^{−2a−4b−2c}, i.e. ⟨J(γ)γ,…⟩ = ⟨γx^{−(a+2b+c)},…⟩, which differs from ⟨γx^{a−c},…⟩ by x^{2(a+b)}; since a+b ≠ 0 these are different rank-3 subgroups (different Z_p-extensions). Moreover the first subgroup is not stable under J (one computes φ(J(γx^{a−c})) = −4(a+b) ≠ 0 in Gal(k_∞/k) ≅ Z_p), so the subsequent claim that "J acts on Gal(k_∞/k) as −1" fails for the group as written; only the second description is J-stable.

The proof announces "Next, we show that p is unramified in k_∞/k", but the argument concludes "So, P_∞Q_∞/k_∞ is an unramified extension, which implies that p is ramified in k_∞/k." The announced goal contradicts the conclusion, and only the latter (ramification in k_∞/k) is what is needed to apply Corollary 2.3.3, whose hypothesis (ii) requires each prime above p to be non-split and ramified in k_∞/k.

predicted_errors.error_location: §3.1.2, end of the proof of Proposition 3.1.7
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: After producing the surjection X'(k_∞) ↠ Gal(L'/k_∞) = ⟨γx^a, xy^{−1}⟩/⟨γx^a,(xy^{−1})^{a+b}⟩, the text twice writes "Gal(L'/k̃)" ("the induced action of J on Gal(L'/k̃) is trivial … J actually acts on Gal(L'/k̃) = ⟨xy^{−1},γx^a⟩/⟨(xy^{−1})^{a+b},γx^a⟩ as −1"). L' is an extension of k_∞ contained in k̃, so Gal(L'/k̃) is meaningless; the displayed quotient is Gal(L'/k_∞), the group to which Corollary 2.3.3 applies.

Lemma 3.1.9's proof states Gal(L_0/k^{(1)}) ≅ X(k^{(1)})^{Gal(k^{(1)}/k)} (invariants) and then deduces X(k^{(1)})=0 "by Nakayama's lemma"; Nakayama applies to coinvariants X_G, not invariants X^G (X^G=0 does not imply X=0). Similarly before Lemma 3.1.11 the text writes "Gal(L_2/k^{(2)}) is isomorphic to X(k̃)^{Gal(k̃/k^{(2)})}", while a few lines later the same object is correctly described as "Gal(L_2/k̃) ≅ X(k̃)_{Gal(k̃/k^{(2)})}" (coinvariants, and over k̃, not k^{(2)}). These statements are mutually inconsistent.

The introduction cites "Fujii [5], Shinkawa [27] and Murakami [21]", but reference [27] is listed as "T. Shirakawa, Generalized Greenberg conjecture for imaginary quadratic fields, Master's thesis, Keio University, 2012". The author's name is given inconsistently, so one of the two is incorrect.
